Welcome to The Constance Bridgeman Centre
The Constance Bridgeman Centre (CBC) is a place where we believe in the potential of every student. Our mission is to provide a supportive and engaging learning environment for young people who have become disaffected with school or exhibit challenging behaviour. We are committed to helping our students develop the skills, knowledge, and confidence they need to succeed in life.
At CBC, we understand that each student is unique and has individual needs. Our dedicated staff are passionate about working with young people and are committed to providing personalised support and guidance. We strive to create a positive and inclusive atmosphere where students feel safe, valued, and empowered.
We believe that education is the key to unlocking opportunities for our students. Through our high-quality educational programs, we aim to help students develop their academic skills, improve their behaviour, and build their self-esteem. We also focus on developing their social and emotional skills, helping them to understand and manage their emotions effectively.
Our commitment to providing a supportive and engaging learning environment will help our students achieve their goals and build a brighter future.
Our mission is to deliver high-quality education that improves life chances, fosters self-awareness, and promotes self-regulation. This commitment drives everything we do, ensuring that every student is supported to maximise their potential and achieve a brighter future.
Our Students
Students attending The Constance Bridgeman Centre often face a range of complex challenges that have impacted their ability to thrive in a mainstream school setting. These challenges can, but are not limited to:
CBC aims to provide a specialised environment to address these challenges and support students re-engaging with their education. We offer smaller class sizes, tailored curriculum, and a focus on social and emotional wellbeing.

Our Ethos, Vision and Values
CBC, where understanding inspires change, belief is nurtured, opportunities are created, and growth is achieved.
Together we grow, learn and achieve.
We strive to eliminate barriers that might hinder a student’s progress, equipping them for success beyond the classroom. Through relentless encouragement, we build resilience, fostering the determination to overcome setbacks, recognise and regulate emotions in order to make sensible decisions and achieve their goals.
We want our students to develop confidence, a positive mindset and have the necessary perseverance to become successful members of society, to respect others, and aspire to achieve.

“Knowledge. Understanding. Opportunity.”
The Constance Bridgeman Centre (CBC) is a Key Stage 4 Pupil Referral Unit (PRU) serving students aged 14 to 16 who have been excluded or referred due to social, emotional, and behavioural challenges. As the main PRU for Years 10 and 11 in the London Borough of Redbridge, we provide a nurturing and supportive environment where students can make a fresh start in a genuinely different learning setting.
With a maximum class size of eight, we foster an ethos of mutual respect and personalised support. Our dedicated staff not only deliver academic opportunities but also provide positive role modelling and guidance to help students navigate various social situations and develop essential life skills.
We operate from an outstanding facility tailored to meet the diverse needs of our students. Referrals are typically made through the Redbridge School Exclusions Team and we can accommodate up to forty students at any one time.

Music at CBC
At CBC, the music curriculum intends to cultivate students’ musical abilities with a particular emphasis on new and innovative technologies alongside traditional instrumentation. By integrating cutting-edge tools and techniques, it is intended that students are exposed to a dynamic and modern musical experience and will foster a well-rounded understanding of music, whilst having the independence to explore particular areas of interest. This curriculum intends to inspire creativity, encourage experimentation, and prepare students for the diverse landscape of contemporary music, promoting a lifelong appreciation for musical expression.
Sessions take place Monday to Thursday 13.30-14.25 and all students take part in one of these sessions per week, with targeted additional withdrawals on an individual basis at arranged times from 11.30-13.00. Further sessions take place on Friday mornings for specific identified members of the cohort.
While currently a non-accreditation course, we are working towards offering NCFE Certificate in Music Technology.
Our approach to music aims to build self-confidence by giving students an opportunity to showcase and perform their music for each other and for staff on a regular basis. Students are put forward for external opportunities such as the pan-London Boroughs United event

Enrichment
At The Constance Bridgeman Centre (CBC), our Enrichment Curriculum is designed to give students opportunities to experience activities and learning beyond the traditional classroom. Many of these experiences may be ones that students would not typically have access to outside of school, helping to broaden their interests and develop new skills.
Through enrichment activities, students are encouraged to build confidence, strengthen relationships, and develop important social and communication skills. The programme supports students in improving their self-esteem while creating opportunities to form positive friendships and work collaboratively with others.
All enrichment activities are carefully selected or designed to reflect and promote the school’s core values: Respect, inclusivity, aspiration, determination and resilience.
Our enrichment offer is reviewed each year and may change depending on the individual needs and interests of our students to ensure that the programme contributes meaningfully to their personal development.
Students take part in foundation-level barbering sessions, delivered by experienced professionals. These sessions introduce students to the core skills of barbering, including hygiene, client care, basic cutting techniques and professional presentation.
The course provides students with a practical insight into the industry and an opportunity to develop focus, precision and creativity in a structured environment. For many, it serves as a platform to explore potential career pathways and further training within the hair and beauty sector.
Barbering at CBC supports employability and independence by helping students gain transferable skills such as communication, attention to detail and customer service. It also promotes confidence and pride in achievement, giving students a valuable foundation should they wish to pursue barbering as a future profession.
Students at CBC take part in structured cycling sessions that focus on building endurance, coordination and confidence. Beginning with mountain biking, students develop control, balance and awareness while navigating a range of terrains. These sessions promote fitness, determination and resilience in a challenging but supportive environment.
As students progress, they move on to advanced cycling sessions at the Olympic Velodrome, where the emphasis shifts towards speed, precision and performance. Training in a world-class facility helps students to refine their technique, set personal goals and experience achievement through focus and perseverance.
Cycling and velodrome training together encourage independence, responsibility and healthy lifestyle habits, providing students with practical skills they can use well beyond their time at CBC.
Climbing reintroduces students to controlled physical challenge and requires focus, courage and trust. In Key Stage 4, students progress to top-rope climbing, developing advanced techniques that demand balance, planning and co-operation with their climbing partner. The experience mirrors many of the personal qualities valued at CBC, resilience, determination and mutual respect and offers an opportunity for pupils to experience achievement through perseverance.
Fairlop Waters – Water Sports
At Fairlop Waters, students participate in a range of water sports including sailing, canoeing and paddle boarding. These experiences build upon earlier teamwork and trust-based activities, requiring calm decision-making and a measured response to changing conditions. Students learn to manage both their physical and emotional responses, developing resilience, problem-solving and communication skills. These activities are key in helping pupils build confidence in unfamiliar environments while enjoying the wellbeing benefits of being outdoors.
Gym and Fitness Training
Students take part in structured gym sessions at a professional fitness facility, applying the routines and techniques introduced during earlier enrichment experiences. The sessions promote the importance of physical health, goal-setting and personal discipline. Working in a public environment also helps students develop independence, confidence and respect for shared spaces, reinforcing the transferable skills they will need as adults.
Redbridge Sports Centre – Racket Sport
Students attend enrichment sessions at Redbridge Sports Centre, where they take part in a range of racket sports including badminton and indoor tennis. These activities help students develop coordination, agility and focus, while also strengthening communication and teamwork skills.
Racket sports encourage students to think strategically, show respect for opponents and demonstrate perseverance through practice and competition. The sessions promote physical fitness and self-discipline, while reinforcing CBC’s core values of effort, respect and resilience. Students gain confidence as they improve their skills and experience the satisfaction of achievement through commitment and teamwork.
Self-Defence and Boxing
Self-defence and boxing sessions at CBC promote confidence, discipline and self-awareness. Students are taught practical techniques for personal safety, self-protection and fitness, alongside strategies for de-escalation and emotional control.
Boxing is delivered in a structured, non-contact format that focuses on skill, co-ordination and resilience rather than aggression. Students learn the importance of respect, routine and self-discipline, while developing strength, stamina and focus through controlled physical activity.
Skiing and Snowboarding
In Year 10, students participate in dry-slope skiing lessons at Brentwood, where they develop balance, co-ordination and focus. These sessions require persistence, patience and determination as students learn to control movement and manage risk in a new and challenging environment.
In Year 11, students progress to snowboarding, applying and extending the skills gained through skiing. This advanced activity promotes further resilience, adaptability and confidence as students take on new physical and technical challenges.
Together, skiing and snowboarding provide unique opportunities for personal growth, encouraging students to persevere, regulate emotions and celebrate success through effort and commitment. Both activities form an integral part of CBC’s wider personal development framework, promoting independence and self-belief.

Careers Information and Guidance (CEIAG)
At CBC, we strive to equip all students with the tools they need for successful careers through a wide-ranging program of careers education, information, advice, and guidance. We firmly believe that outstanding careers education is one of the driving forces behind social mobility and therefore our aspiring careers programme is an integral part of the offer provided to our students.
Throughout Year 10-11 all students will have had the opportunity to:
Prepare CVs and application forms
Gain a comprehensive understanding of post-16 options
Career Guidance Meetings
Students are entitled to appropriate guidance to meet their individual needs. All pupils at school can request an appointment with the CEIAG Co-ordinator, although Year 10 & 11 will have scheduled half-termly appointments. Students are identified for careers meetings based on need and through self-referral.
Career Information
Career information is available through relevant displays and through assemblies. Students at CBC will have access to a range of career guides, apprenticeship and employer information, as well as guides on job-search activities.
External Providers
Ranges of external providers are invited into school to support the careers programme. These might include local colleges, universities, training providers, apprenticeship organisations, employers, school alumni, or staff from various projects.
Employer Links
Links with employers, businesses and other external agencies continue to grow by building on local community connections with a view to offer pupils experience in the world of work.
For all information regarding Careers Education and the schools Career Programme, please contact Olia Clow cbcadmin@nrhs.redbridge.sch.uk

Referrals
Students are referred to CBC through the Redbridge Local Authority Schools Exclusion Team. These referrals can be due to permanent exclusions from mainstream schools or fixed-term referrals when a student is at risk of exclusion.
We do not accept direct referrals from private individuals. However, we are able to accept students from outside the Redbridge Local Authority, as well as transfers from other Pupil Referral Units (PRUs). All applications should be initially made via Redbridge Schools Exclusion Team.
Potential students and their parent/carer(s) are referred to the Redbridge Inclusion Panel by an appropriate agency, and from there they may be referred to a Pupil Referral Unit.
CBC is one of two PRUs serving Key Stage 4 students in Redbridge. We are committed to providing every student with the opportunity to receive an education and a fresh start. However, students must be willing to engage and work with us to develop acceptable behaviour and learning practices in order to succeed.
All prospective Key Stage 4 students and their parent/carer(s) are invited to attend an initial interview, followed by a diagnostic baseline assessment. This assessment identifies areas of the literacy and numeracy curriculum that may need additional support. Following this, students are allocated to a tutor group and provided with a daily timetable.
Students who are well placed within our environment typically attend regularly, follow our common-sense rules, and achieve success. If there are concerns about behaviour, punctuality, or attendance, an early review meeting will be arranged to support the individual student and ensure they stay on track. Our priority is to maintain a calm, focused learning atmosphere for all students. It is also important that staff are able to work in a safe and positive environment.

Pastoral Care
At CBC we recognise that students make the best academic progress when their emotional and social needs are met. Accordingly, we provide comprehensive pastoral care.
When a student begins work with us, they benefit from an initial, intensive meeting with our dedicated Pastoral, Behaviour & Welfare Lead who uses this time to assess their individual care needs. Resulting from this we can offer a diverse range of supportive interventions and intense wrap-around pastoral care.
It is our firm belief that through the interventions indicated and by providing warm, caring, and supportive environment, we can maximise the academic success, happiness, well-being and future life-chances of each student in our care.

Additional Support
At the CBC, we provide a comprehensive range of additional support to help our students thrive both academically and personally.
Literacy Mentor
All students are withdrawn for individual support sessions on a weekly basis with our Literacy Mentor. The aim is to provide personally targeted literacy and language support to consolidate achievement in English.
Behaviour Mentor
All students are given individual support from our Behaviour Mentor. The aim is to provide personally targeted assistance to enable students to reflect and consider ways in which they could better manage their behaviour in the future in order to raise their achievement overall.
Careers Support
Our Careers Advisor visits on a fortnightly basis to provide individual support and advice to our students regarding post-16 options.
Health Advisor
Our EOTAS Health Advisor visits regularly and offers advice and support to students on a variety of health issues.
Safer Schools Officer
We have an allocated police liaison officer who visits regularly to engage with students and develop positive relationships, as well as offer specific police support and intervention should it prove necessary.

This commitment extends to all members of our school community, including staff, parents, and volunteers.

Curriculum
Teaching, learning and assessment embedded in the curriculum here, at The Constance Bridgeman Centre, aims to ensure that, by the end of their journey with us, all learners know more, understand the world around them and are provided with an opportunity to achieve academic and personal goals.
Students can study a variety of subjects:
Here at CBC, we strive to provide a rich and balanced curriculum which engages learners with education and broadens their understanding of the world around them, as well as preparing them for the future ahead. We make sure that every child is taught the knowledge they need to grasp opportunities and be successful in their next stage of education, employment and adult life.
We continuously review and reshape our curriculum to meet the diverse and ever-changing needs of our students, incorporating their past experiences and individualised needs. Through our offer and high-quality teaching and pedagogy practice we strive to develop, deepen and secure not only academic knowledge, but also soft skills, necessary to become well-rounded individuals and positive members of society. Through our curriculum and learning experiences we aim to develop creativity, communication skills, problem solving, self-management and cultural awareness as well as many other skills we believe are essential for successful life and achievement.
Regular formative low stakes ‘assessment for learning’ takes place throughout lessons to address common misconceptions and provide immediate feedback that supports understanding and progress, as well as supporting future planning that incorporates students’ needs. Though open dialog we practice teachers are able to assess understanding and address areas that may need further explanation. Our teachers are well equipped in the knowledge and skill of breaking down academic content, making it accessible for every individual student that attends school. Teaching is designed to engage learners and develops their knowledge providing not only equality of education but equity of achievement and progress.

Understanding
Learners are at the centre of our practice here at CBC; our ethos and vision of mutual respect is evident not only through our curriculum design and approaches to teaching and learning, but also through all activities within the school. Small class sizes allow for opportunities to develop positive relationships between students and staff to support academic progress as well as emotional well-being and social awareness.
All our staff have a deep understanding of students’ personal journeys and barriers to learning, and work tirelessly to overcome those in order to build relationships, reach academic success, and support learners through this stage of their educational journey.
Teachers’ broad understanding and knowledge of how students learn, allows for creation of truly personal learning plans and offers which are accessible and realistic, allowing students to build on and improve their academic and social self-esteem.
Our curriculum and approaches to teaching and learning are created with the understanding of learners’ needs and are designed to support not only academic progress, but also students’ personal aspirations and ambitions. It is our belief that only by understanding our past journey and experiences can we shape our future.
Opportunity
Students that come through our doors and join our community have been permanently excluded or are at risk of exclusion from mainstream education. Those students often have a negative view of education or have been disengaged from any form of education for some time. It is therefore important to re-engage, excite and motivate them with education as a whole.
In order to achieve that, we provide every student with an opportunity to express their views, wants and desires. Student voice is an important part of our curriculum design as well as teaching and learning practices throughout the school. We do not only listen to our learners, but hear what they are saying and respect their views and opinions.
By working with our learners, we provide them with opportunities that may not have been available for them in other settings. Opportunities not only to achieve academic success, but to explore their interests, develop their creativity and explore possibilities of different career pathways for the future.

Cultural Capital
Cultural Capital refers to the key knowledge, experiences and opportunities that help pupils become well-rounded and informed members of society. It introduces pupils to important ideas, creativity and achievements, helping them to understand and appreciate the world around them.
At The Constance Bridgeman Centre (CBC), we place great value on ensuring that pupils have access to a wide range of opportunities that enrich their learning and personal development. Cultural Capital is developed through educational visits, trips and experiences linked to different areas of the curriculum, allowing pupils to explore learning beyond the classroom.
In addition to curriculum-based visits, pupils benefit from themed weeks, celebrations, reward trips, and a variety of engaging activities. These opportunities are designed to broaden pupils’ horizons and allow them to participate in experiences they may not usually encounter.
Our Cultural Capital programme is carefully planned so that experiences build progressively each year, helping pupils to develop their understanding of the world and supporting them in becoming confident, thoughtful and active members of their communities. Subject Intent
English
In Year 11 the English curriculum encourages students to develop strong literacy skills through the study of a wide variety of texts and literary forms. Students learn to analyse ideas, communicate effectively and develop their own voice in both spoken and written work.
By exploring different themes and perspectives, students gain a deeper understanding of English language while building a lifelong appreciation for reading and writing. The skills develop are critical for students to attain a recognise qualification and gain entry to a chosen career pathway.
Mathematics
In Year 11 the mathematics curriculum focuses on strengthening students’ confidence and accuracy in applying mathematical concepts. Students continue to develop reasoning skills, problem-solving strategies and the ability to apply mathematics to real-life situations.
The course supports students in achieving recognised qualifications while ensuring they gain essential numerical skills needed for everyday life and future employment.
Science
In Year 11 the science curriculum continues to develop students’ scientific understanding and build on their prior knowledge while developing investigative skills through practical work and data analysis. All three disciplines physic, chemistry and biology are taught with the aim with all students attaining GCSE qualification or equivalent. Lessons encourage students to question ideas, test hypotheses and evaluate results, helping them develop a deeper understanding of the scientific world and potential future pathways in science-related fields.
Art
In Year 11 the art curriculum enables students to further refine their artistic skills and develop personal creative projects. They are encouraged to experiment with materials and techniques while developing their own artistic style and ideas.
Students also analyse and interpret the work of artists and designers, helping them understand the role of art in society and the range of creative career opportunities available. Students will be prepared for a recognised GCSE qualification or equivalent.
Food Technology
In Year 11 the Food Technology curriculum is designed to enable students to explore the art of cooking and food innovation in a practical and engaging way. With a strong emphasis on hands-on learning, students develop essential skills in food preparation, cooking techniques, and an understanding of the nutritional value of ingredients.
The curriculum combines practical experiences with underpinning theoretical knowledge, allowing students to understand where food comes from, how it contributes to a healthy lifestyle, and how to plan and produce a range of dishes safely and effectively.
Through this balanced approach, students gain the skills and knowledge required to access an appropriate qualification pathway, whether that be a BTEC Level 2 or a GCSE qualification, supporting their individual strengths and future aspirations.
Music
In Year 11 the Music curriculum allows students to further develop their performance and composition skills while exploring the technical and creative aspects of music production.
Students gain practical experience in creating and recording music while continuing to build knowledge of the music industry. Through their studies, students work towards achieving their BTEC Music qualification.
Physical Education (PE)
In Year 11 the PE curriculum continues to promote participation, fitness and teamwork through a variety of sporting activities. Students further develop their physical abilities while strengthening confidence, resilience and cooperation.
The curriculum aims to support students in maintaining an active lifestyle and developing skills that can be applied in both recreational and competitive settings.
PSHE / RSE
In Year 11 the PSHE curriculum focuses on preparing students for adulthood by exploring topics such as healthy relationships, personal wellbeing, financial responsibility, employment and future education pathways.
Through discussion and practical learning activities, students develop the confidence to make informed decisions and understand the responsibilities of adult life. Religious Education remains part of the programme, helping students develop respect for different cultures, beliefs and communities.
Parents retain the legal right to withdraw their child from the sex education component of the RSE curriculum.

Year 10 Curriculum
At The Constance Bridgeman Centre (CBC), the Year 10 curriculum is designed to provide students with a broad, balanced and engaging programme of study that supports both academic achievement and personal development. Our aim is to ensure that students are given the opportunity to develop their abilities, build confidence and prepare for future pathways through gaining recognised qualifications.
Please click on the links below to get more information as to what students will be studying across each curriculum each 1/2 term:
Subject Intent
English
The Key Stage 4 English curriculum focuses on the development of English Language skills, enabling students to become confident communicators and effective readers. Through studying a range of texts and real-world materials, students learn how to interpret information, share their ideas clearly and communicate appropriately with different audiences.
The curriculum prioritises the development of core literacy skills, including reading comprehension, writing accuracy and spoken communication. Students are supported in structuring their ideas clearly, improving their vocabulary and expressing their thoughts with confidence. By building these essential skills, we aim to prepare students for further education, employment and everyday life.
Mathematics
The Key Stage 4 Mathematics curriculum focuses on equipping students with the knowledge and confidence to use mathematical skills in everyday situations and future employment. The curriculum encourages students to develop fluency, logical thinking and effective problem-solving strategies.
Through structured learning and practice, students learn how to apply mathematical reasoning, select appropriate methods and solve a range of problems. Our aim is for every student, regardless of starting point, to make strong progress and achieve qualifications that support their future ambitions.
Science
The Key Stage 4 Science curriculum aims to develop students’ curiosity about the world while strengthening their ability to think critically and work independently. Students investigate key scientific concepts through hands-on activities and practical learning, helping them to understand how scientific ideas apply to everyday life.
Lessons provide opportunities for students to carry out investigations, form predictions, analyse evidence and draw conclusions from their findings. Through studying Combined Science GCSE, students gradually build their scientific knowledge while also developing important skills such as problem solving, resilience and analytical thinking, preparing them for further learning and future career pathways.
Art
The Key Stage 4 Art curriculum encourages students to develop creativity, resilience and independent thinking. Students explore a variety of artistic techniques, materials and processes while developing their own ideas and creative style.
Students learn about both historical and contemporary artists, helping them to understand how art reflects culture and society. The course also introduces students to the wide range of careers and opportunities available within the creative industries.
Food Technology
The Key Stage 4 Food Technology curriculum is designed to enable students to explore the art of cooking and food innovation in a practical and engaging way. With a strong emphasis on hands-on learning, students develop essential skills in food preparation, cooking techniques, and an understanding of the nutritional value of ingredients.
The curriculum combines practical experiences with underpinning theoretical knowledge, allowing students to understand where food comes from, how it contributes to a healthy lifestyle, and how to plan and produce a range of dishes safely and effectively.
Through this balanced approach, students gain the skills and knowledge required to access an appropriate qualification pathway, whether that be a BTEC Level 2 or a GCSE qualification, supporting their individual strengths and future aspirations.
Music
The Key Stage 4 Music curriculum intends to not only focus on helping students to express themselves creatively through performance and composition but also includes preparing students for music industry careers. This comprehensive program ensures students not only cultivate a thorough understanding of music but also acquire practical skills, providing them with the essential knowledge for successful endeavours in the dynamic music industry. The curriculum aims to empower students with a well-rounded musical education that prepares them for a variety of opportunities and challenges; all whilst gaining a BTEC qualification.
Physical Education (PE)
The Key Stage 4 PE curriculum is based on the principle of “Sport for All”, ensuring that every student has the opportunity to participate and enjoy physical activity. Through a range of sports and activities, students develop physical fitness, teamwork and confidence.
Lessons are designed to improve physical ability as well as social and mental wellbeing. Students are encouraged to apply their skills in different sporting situations, including competitive activities, while building resilience and teamwork.
PSHE / RSE
The Key Stage 4 Personal, Social, Health and Economic Education (PSHE) curriculum helps students develop the knowledge and life skills needed to become healthy, responsible and confident adults.
Students explore topics such as relationships, wellbeing, financial awareness, future careers and decision-making. Lessons encourage discussion, reflection and understanding of different viewpoints, helping students to develop respect for others.
Religious Education is also included within the PSHE curriculum, supporting students in developing awareness and respect for different faiths, beliefs and cultures.
This curriculum ensures students are prepared for life in a diverse and modern society.
Parents have the statutory right to withdraw their child from the sex education element of the RSE curriculum.

A Message From Our Headteacher
We at Constance Bridgeman Centre (CBC) are delighted to welcome you to our school community. As the new Headteacher, I am honoured to join a team that plays such a vital role in helping young people re-engage with learning, rebuild their confidence, and move forward positively.
At CBC, we understand that every young person’s journey is unique. Many of our pupils have faced significant challenges in previous settings, and we believe it is our shared responsibility and privilege to meet them with empathy, high expectations, and genuine care. Together, we place strong, positive relationships at the heart of everything we do.
Our goal is to create an inclusive, supportive, and purposeful environment where every young person is empowered to become the best version of themselves. We know this work is only successful when we collaborate closely with families. Your voice, experiences, and partnership are incredibly important to us, and we warmly welcome open communication between home and school.
We look forward to working alongside you to build a community where every young person feels valued, supported, and inspired to thrive.
Mr Ernest Regisford Headteacher
